saw_lines: A brain device costs real money, so buyers ask about delivery, returns and warranty before they click buy.
So the sale is lost in the first line, where buyers see a saving but not whether the helmet reaches them.
Your 9 of 12 ads open on the same saving line, so run 2 or 3 new opening angles from your helmet against it in the next batch.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 21 Oct 2026
points: 9 of 12 copy ads open on “fancy saving over $500 on...”, so most buyers meet one reason to buy. Test 2 or 3 new angles against it, such as the 10 to 30 minute daily routine and the caregiver story.

Your site offers worldwide free shipping, yet 0 of 12 ads mention shipping or delivery, so new buyers get no answer to their first question. Put free worldwide delivery in the first line of ads aimed at new buyers.

One exact copy runs in 9 of 12 ads, so most of your account repeats a single message with little change. Keep the copy but change the opening line and the creative in each ad so every version reads as new.
None of your 12 ads carries a proof number, so a new buyer has nothing concrete to hold onto. Collect one figure, such as your review count or orders shipped, and open the next batch with it.

ads_1: New helmet openers on daily routine and caregivers, tested against the saving hook
